title: In-app toast for non-obvious gameplay events
description:
Replace ephemeral Alert.alert() calls with a non-blocking in-app toast/banner for gameplay events that don't require user interaction.

## Architecture

Drive toasts off the SSE stream (mobile/src/hooks/useGameplayEvents.ts), NOT the push notification payload. Rationale:
- SSE is already delivering every event in real-time while the app is foregrounded.
- iOS/Android suppress push notifications by default while an app is foregrounded, so there's no overlap/dedup concern between the toast and a push banner.
- This is why the 'enable in-app notifications' prompt pattern is unnecessary here — those apps lack a realtime channel and reuse push payloads; we have SSE.

## Toast Component

- **Custom Reanimated banner** (~100 lines) — no new native deps, full control over styling.
- **Top-of-screen**, design-language colors (not system toast styling).
- **Single visible + queue depth 1** — if a second event arrives while one is showing, it waits; no history.
- **5s auto-dismiss**, swipe-to-dismiss, tap-to-dismiss.
- No tap-to-navigate (none of the scoped events require action).

## Rule of Thumb

**Toast when the screen stays. Alert when the screen changes.**
- Events that leave the player on the gameplay screen → toast.
- Events that navigate the player away (self-kick → home, game end → recap) → keep the blocking Alert (or just navigate) since toasts would race screen transitions.
- Events that already open a dedicated UI (FoundClaimModal) → no change.
- Confirmation-style Alerts (veto/abandon/kick/end game/power-up/set-stop) → stay modal — they require user action.

## Events Migrating to Toasts

| Event | Audience | Copy |
|---|---|---|
| `player_left` (other player) | all same-role peers | `"<Name> has left the game"` or `"<Name> was removed by the host"` |
| `host_changed` (new host) | new host only | `"You are the new host"` |
| `host_changed` (others) | all other players | `"<Name> has been made the new host"` |
| `hiding_zone_expanded` | all (including the initiating hider — toast doubles as action feedback) | `"The hiding zone has been expanded to <new radius>"` |
| `proximity_escalated` | hider (channel-gated, already hider-only) | existing strings from `proximityEscalationMessage`, no title |
| `proximity_deescalated` | hider (channel-gated, already hider-only) | existing strings from `proximityDeescalationMessage`, no title |
| `found_claim_rejected` | seeker | `"The hiders rejected your found claim"` |
| `found_claim_expired` | both roles | `"The found claim timed out"` |

New radius for `hiding_zone_expanded`: compute on mobile from `useGameInfo` base radius × 2, formatted per the game's `DistanceConvention` (km / mi).

## Events NOT Changing

- **Self-kick** (`player_left` where `player_id === playerId`): keep the blocking Alert. Screen transitions to home immediately after; a toast would race navigation and be lost.
- **`FoundClaimModal`** (driven by `found_claim` event): already a dedicated pageSheet modal; not an Alert.
- **Confirmation-style Alerts** (veto/abandon/kick/end game/power-up confirms/set-stop confirm): remain modal because they require user decisions.
- **Question lifecycle events** (asked/answered/vetoed/abandoned): already have clear visual affordances (question banner, thermometer, map overlays) — no toast needed.
- **Phase transitions, game_started, game_dissolved, game_ended**: navigation covers these.

## Current State

`mobile/src/hooks/useGameplayEvents.ts` is the only dispatch point to modify. The events above are all currently handled there.

## History

Originally beads-466 (general notification queueing). Narrowed after brainstorming revealed most events already have visual affordances. beads-466 closed as superseded.

title: Seeker question history scrubber with exclusion replay
description:
Add a utility belt entry for seekers that opens a modal with a scrubber/timeline over answered questions.

## Where it lives

mobile/src/components/utility-belt/UtilityBelt.tsx — the seeker utility belt already holds 'Endgame' (opens QuestionCutoffModal). Add the 'History' entry alongside.

## Modal contents

- Standalone mini-map rendering transit lines, stations, and game boundary (independent of the main map — safe to render without affecting main game state).
- At the current scrub position:
  - Cumulative exclusion *through* that point: rendered in red see-through (union of all exclusion deltas from Q1 through current).
  - The scrubbed-to question's *delta* exclusion: rendered in solid question-color, NOT drawn under already-excluded regions. The solid area visually encodes the marginal information value of that specific question — a tiny solid area means the question told us little new; a large area means it narrowed things significantly.
- Question card below scrubber showing type/params/answer at current position (reuse QuestionHistoryRow where appropriate).
- Scrubber is view-only — unlike the endgame cutoff modal, no exclusion setting/cutoff.

## Implementation concern: rendering the delta

'Delta exclusion not drawn under already-excluded regions' is a non-trivial client-side geometry operation (PostGIS ST_Difference equivalent). Candidates:
- @turf/difference — likely already available or easy to add; works on GeoJSON.
- Naive z-ordering (draw cumulative, then draw delta on top) will NOT achieve the effect — colors blend visibly and the cumulative shows through the delta. Must actually subtract geometries before rendering.

## Reference implementation

mobile/src/components/QuestionCutoffModal.tsx already renders a map with exclusion overlays — study its exclusion layer rendering before starting.

## Data source

SeekerQuestionAnsweredEvent carries per-question exclusion geometry; already on client via GameplayStore.question_history. No new endpoints.

## Edge cases

- Empty state: no answered questions yet → show friendly empty message, hide scrubber.
- Single question: scrubber collapses to a single position.
- Scrub to position 0 (before any questions): show boundary + map only, no exclusions.
- Vetoed/abandoned questions: no exclusion geometry — decide whether to include as scrubber stops (likely yes for completeness, but render with no delta overlay).

title: DB-backed timer reconciler to replace Celery ETA for game timers
description:
Game phase transitions (hiding→seeking) and question auto-answers are currently scheduled via Celery's apply_async(countdown=...). This is fragile: Celery's Redis broker hands ETA tasks to a worker immediately, and the worker holds the timer in memory until fire-time. If the worker crashes/restarts/OOMs between scheduling and firing, the timer is lost — with a 180min hiding phase, that's a long uptime requirement for a single request. Redis AOF persistence doesn't help because the task is no longer in Redis.

Fix: stop using Celery ETA. Authoritative fire-times already live in Postgres (Game.hiding_started_at + hiding_time_min, Question.answerable_at). Add a periodic tick (~1s) that queries for overdue rows and enqueues immediate Celery tasks. Celery becomes a worker pool only (what it's good at), never a scheduler. A late restart means timers fire N seconds late, never lost.

Deployment: run Celery Beat as a new docker-compose service alongside api + worker. Beat publishes a 'reconcile_timers' periodic task every 1s; the existing worker picks it up and executes reconciliation using existing Python logic (logic/, broadcast/). Beat is tiny (~50MB, single-purpose), and if it dies for N seconds timers are merely N seconds late.

Rejected alternatives:
- pg_cron inside Postgres — can detect due timers in SQL but can't execute transitions (logic is Python: emit events, clean up locations, send pushes). Would still need a Python consumer, so no simplicity gain.
- Background task inside API server — multiple API replicas would duplicate fires without advisory locks, and API restart cadence would affect timer cadence.
- Inside the Celery worker itself — same SPOF we're trying to escape.

Transitions must be idempotent (double-tick guard — check current status before acting) so a redundant tick after the real one already fired is a no-op.

Call sites to migrate:
- server/src/hideandseek/routers/games.py:332 (transition_hiding_to_seeking)
- server/src/hideandseek/routers/questions.py:82 (auto_answer_question)
close_reason: Implemented in 82631b9: hideandseek-reconciler package polls Postgres every 1s for overdue timers and enqueues existing Celery tasks; routers no longer schedule or revoke.

title: Scheduled hider actions: queue veto/randomize before auto-answer deadline
description:
Allow hiders to pre-schedule a powerup action (veto or randomize) in response to a question, so they can take maximum strategic time without risking the auto-answer timer firing before they act.

When a question becomes answerable, the hider has three choices:
1. Answer immediately
2. Wait and answer/play powerup manually before the timer expires
3. Schedule a powerup action — the server holds it and executes it just before the auto-answer would fire

This is important because the hider may want to use the full timer duration strategically (e.g. to move to a better position) but can't risk the auto-answer resolving the question normally.

Key design points:
- New endpoint: POST /questions/{id}/schedule-action with action type (veto/randomize).
- Scheduled action replaces the auto-answer task — if the hider doesn't answer manually before the deadline, the scheduled powerup fires instead of auto-answer.
- Hider can cancel a scheduled action and answer normally instead.
- If hider answers manually before the deadline, the scheduled action is discarded.
- Depends on veto and randomize powerups being implemented first.
close_reason: Scheduled veto implemented via ?scheduled=true on veto endpoint. Auto-answer task checks scheduled_veto flag and vetoes instead of computing answer. Scheduled randomize deferred until randomize powerup (HideAndSeek-fcz) lands.

title: Early hiding zone declaration + ambiguous overlap resolution
description:
Design doc: `design/hider-station-election.md`

Hiders can voluntarily elect their station during the hiding phase, or the system assigns one at the hiding-to-seeking transition. Ambiguity (0 or 2+ valid candidates) is handled via a dedicated status on the game, with fallback resolution when auto-answer timers fire.

## Key Decisions (from design doc)
- One station per game (hiders travel as a group)
- Election is permanent — no revocation
- All hiders must be within hiding_zone_radius of the elected stop (not just centroid)
- No timing restriction on election
- StationElectionStatus enum: pending | elected | auto_assigned | ambiguous
- Questions blocked while ambiguous; auto-answer fallback resolves first

## Fallback Resolution Cascade
1. All-hiders-in-radius → tightest fit
2. Any-hider-in-radius → shortest min distance
3. Closest (stop, hider) pair

## Endpoints
- GET /nearby-stations?lat=&lng= — stateless, open to all, includes hiding zone polygons
- POST /hider-station — hider-only, permanent election
- GET /hiding-zone?station_id= — open to all, pure geometry query
- GET /hider-station (existing) — extended with station_election_status

title: Auto-sync SSE event types via OpenAPI schema injection
description:
## Problem

SSE delta event types are maintained by hand in `mobile/src/types/gameplay.ts` (~200 lines) and can silently drift from the server's event dataclasses in `server/src/hideandseek/broadcast/events.py`. REST endpoint types are already auto-synced via the `FastAPI → openapi.yaml → openapi-typescript → schema.d.ts` pipeline, but SSE events are excluded because the streaming endpoints use `include_in_schema=False` and the delta events are plain dataclasses, not Pydantic models.

The primary goal is syncing the **delta event types** — the incremental SSE messages like `QuestionAskedEvent`, `PhaseChangedEvent`, `PlayerLocationEvent`, etc. The initial state snapshots (`HiderGameStateResponse`, `SeekerGameStateResponse`) are already Pydantic and can be included easily, but the deltas are the harder and more important part.

## Approach: OpenAPI schema injection (no fake endpoints)

Register SSE event schemas directly into the OpenAPI spec by customizing `app.openapi()` in the FastAPI app. This injects schemas into `components/schemas` without creating fake endpoints. Then `openapi-typescript` picks them up automatically, and the existing pre-commit hook (`openapi-regen.sh` → `api-types-regen.sh`) keeps everything in sync.

### Step 1: Convert delta event dataclasses to Pydantic schemas

The delta events in `broadcast/events.py` are currently frozen dataclasses. They need Pydantic schema counterparts to generate JSON Schema for OpenAPI injection.

**Key design decision**: Where do the Pydantic event schemas live? Options:
- `schemas/events.py` (new file, parallel to `schemas/response.py`) — keeps schemas package consistent
- Keep the dataclasses in `broadcast/events.py` as the internal representation, Pydantic schemas are the wire format definition

**Lobby delta events to model** (from `broadcast/events.py`):
- `PlayerJoinedEvent` — game: GameResponse, player: PlayerResponse
- `PlayerUpdatedEvent` — game: GameResponse, player: PlayerResponse
- `PlayerLeftEvent` — game: GameResponse, player_id: UUID
- `HostChangedEvent` — game: GameResponse, new_host_player_id: UUID
- `GameStartedEvent` — game: GameResponse

**Gameplay delta events to model** (role-specific — this is the critical part):
- `PlayerLocationEvent` — game_id, player_id, name, color, role, coordinates (GeoJSON Point), timestamp
- `QuestionAskedEvent` — game_id, question_id, question_type, status, asked_by, slot_index, parameters (RadarEventParams | ThermometerEventParams | FeatureEventParams), seeker_location_start, asked_at, ask_count, sequence
- `QuestionAnswerableEvent` — game_id, question_id, question_type, status, seeker_location_end
- `HiderQuestionAnsweredEvent` — hider-only: includes hider_location, hider feature resolution
- `SeekerQuestionAnsweredEvent` — seeker-only: includes exclusion geometry, total_exclusion, no hider data
- `QuestionVetoedEvent` — game_id, question_id, question_type, slot_index
- `QuestionAbandonedEvent` — game_id, question_id, question_type, slot_index
- `PhaseChangedEvent` — game_id, phase, seeking_started_at, station_election_status, hider_station_id
- `StationElectionEvent` — game_id, station_election_status, hider_station_id (hider channel only)
- `GamePlayerLeftEvent` — game_id, player_id

**Question parameter sub-types** (already have Pydantic versions in `schemas/params.py`):
- `RadarParamsResponse`, `ThermometerParamsResponse`, `FeatureParamsResponse`, `FeatureResolution`
- The event dataclasses use their own `RadarEventParams`/`ThermometerEventParams`/`FeatureEventParams` — these should converge with or reference the existing Pydantic param schemas

**Important**: Follow the project convention of separate event classes for role-specific payloads (per feedback_separate_event_classes.md). `HiderQuestionAnsweredEvent` and `SeekerQuestionAnsweredEvent` must remain distinct types in the generated schema.

### Step 2: Inject schemas into OpenAPI spec

1. **Customize `app.openapi()`** (in `server/src/hideandseek/app.py` or wherever the FastAPI app is created):
   - Call the base `openapi()` to get the existing schema
   - Use `.model_json_schema()` on each Pydantic event schema
   - Inject into `openapi_schema["components"]["schemas"]`
   - Handle `$defs` — Pydantic's `.model_json_schema()` puts nested types in `$defs`; these need to be hoisted into `components/schemas` or resolved inline so `openapi-typescript` generates named types, not anonymous inlined objects

2. **Also register initial state snapshots** (already Pydantic, easy wins):
   - `HiderGameStateResponse`, `SeekerGameStateResponse`
   - `HiderActiveQuestion`, `SeekerActiveQuestion`
   - `HiderQuestionHistoryEntry`, `SeekerQuestionHistoryEntry`
   - `GamePlayer`, `RosterPlayer`, `StopResponse`, `InventorySlotResponse`

3. **Consider a discriminated union schema** for each channel's event set:
   - `LobbySSEEvent = PlayerJoinedEvent | PlayerUpdatedEvent | ...` with discriminator on event type
   - `HiderSSEEvent = PlayerLocationEvent | QuestionAskedEvent | HiderQuestionAnsweredEvent | ...`
   - `SeekerSSEEvent = PlayerLocationEvent | QuestionAskedEvent | SeekerQuestionAnsweredEvent | ...`
   - This gives the mobile side a single union type to parse against per channel

### Step 3: Update mobile to use generated types

4. **Replace hand-written types** in `mobile/src/types/gameplay.ts` with imports from `@/api/schema.d.ts`
   - Generated types will be under `components["schemas"]["EventName"]` etc.
   - May want a thin re-export file for ergonomic imports

5. **Update consumers**:
   - `useGameplayEvents.ts` — event parsing and store hydration
   - `useLobbyEvents.ts` — event parsing and cache updates
   - `GameplayStore` and any components importing from `gameplay.ts`

### Validation

6. Diff generated types against current hand-written `gameplay.ts` to catch any existing drift
7. Run mobile typecheck (`npx tsc --noEmit`) to verify all consumers compile
8. Manual test: connect to SSE endpoints, verify events parse correctly with generated types

## Files involved

- `server/src/hideandseek/broadcast/events.py` — existing event dataclasses (internal representation, stays)
- `server/src/hideandseek/schemas/events.py` — **new**: Pydantic schemas for SSE events (wire format)
- `server/src/hideandseek/schemas/response.py` — existing response schemas (also to be registered)
- `server/src/hideandseek/schemas/params.py` — existing question parameter schemas
- `server/src/hideandseek/app.py` — OpenAPI customization hook
- `server/scripts/generate_openapi.py` — verify it picks up custom schemas
- `mobile/src/types/gameplay.ts` — to be replaced by generated types
- `mobile/src/hooks/useGameplayEvents.ts` — update imports
- `mobile/src/hooks/useLobbyEvents.ts` — update imports
- `openapi/openapi.yaml` — will gain SSE event component schemas
- `mobile/src/api/schema.d.ts` — will gain SSE types automatically

Many API actions are made by players whose current location is known to the client. Rather than relying solely on the dedicated POST /games/{game_id}/location endpoint, we should accept an optional location field on relevant requests and treat it as an implicit location update.

Candidate endpoints:
- POST /games/{game_id}/questions (seeker asking a question — already needs seeker location)
- POST /games/{game_id}/questions/{id}/lock-in (seeker locking in thermometer — uses latest location)
- POST /games/{game_id}/questions/{id}/answer (hider answering — snapshots hider location)

- Reduces location staleness for critical game actions
- Fewer dedicated location report round-trips needed
- More accurate question answers since location is fresh at the moment of action

- Add optional 'coordinates' (GeoJSON Point) + 'timestamp' fields to relevant request schemas
- When present, create a LocationUpdate before processing the main action
- Use the fresh location instead of querying the latest stored one

title: Extract database models into top-level package for migration support
description:
## Motivation

The server's SQLAlchemy models currently live at `server/src/hideandseek/models/`. When we add Alembic migrations, the migration environment needs to import the model metadata — but it shouldn't need the full server package (FastAPI, Celery, push infra, etc.). Extracting models into a standalone top-level package enables:

1. **Clean migration setup** — Alembic imports only the models package, not the server
2. **Dependency isolation** — models package has minimal deps (SQLAlchemy, GeoAlchemy2, shapely, pyproj, pydantic)
3. **Future reuse** — other tools (data scripts, admin CLI) can depend on models without pulling in the server

## Design

Create a new top-level package (e.g. `models/` or `db/`) with its own `pyproject.toml`. The server references it via UV workspace local dependency (`hideandseek-models = { path = '../models' }`).

### What moves
- `models/base.py` — DeclarativeBase
- `models/types.py` — enums, constants, DistrictClass
- `models/geo_types.py` — custom SQLAlchemy column types (ShapelyGeography, ShapelyGeometry)
- All table model files (game, player, question, transit, etc.)
- `models/__init__.py` — re-exports

### What stays in server
- `db.py` (engine, session management, ContextVar plumbing)
- `queries/` (session-dependent DB access)
- Everything else (routers, logic, schemas, etc.)

### Key decisions
- Package name: TBD (e.g. `hideandseek-models`, `hideandseek-db`)
- The models package should have zero dependency on FastAPI or any server infra
- Import paths change from `hideandseek.models` to the new package name — requires updating all imports across server code
- UV workspace configuration needed at monorepo root

### Dependencies for the new package
- sqlalchemy
- geoalchemy2
- shapely
- pyproj (used by geo_types)
- pydantic (DistrictClass in types.py is a BaseModel)

### Blockers / considerations
- Ensure `Base.metadata` is still discoverable by `create_all()` in server startup
- Test fixtures reference models heavily — imports need updating
- OpenAPI generation script imports models — needs updating
- GTFS/seed scripts import models — needs updating

title: Re-askable questions with escalating cost multiplier
description:
Questions can be asked more than once. Each subsequent ask of the same question costs more — 2x on second ask, 3x on third, etc. This is foundational to the veto and randomize powerups (a vetoed question can be re-asked at multiplied cost, and a randomized original question can be re-asked at its original cost).

Current behavior: asking a question consumes the inventory slot (radar/thermometer) or category usage (matching/measuring) permanently. A consumed slot cannot be reused.

New behavior:
- Slot-based (radar/thermometer): a consumed slot can be re-asked. The cost multiplier determines how many "draws" the hider gets (game mechanic, not server-enforced). The slot's consumed_at is set on first ask; re-asks don't change it.
- Category-based (matching/measuring): a used category can be re-asked. Same multiplier logic.
- Track ask count per (game, question identity) to compute the multiplier. Question identity = slot_index for slot-based, (category, feature_class, question_type) for category-based.
- The "one unanswered question at a time" rule still applies — can't re-ask while the previous instance is pending.
- Vetoed questions reset to re-askable at the current multiplier. Randomized originals reset to re-askable at 1x (original cost).

Open questions:
- Should the multiplier be returned in the ask response so the client can display it?
- How to model ask count — new column on InventorySlot/CategoryUsage, or a separate counter?
- Does the server enforce the cost (e.g. block re-ask if hider hasn't drawn enough cards), or is it trust-based like powerups?
close_reason: Unified InventorySlot model, re-askable slots with ask_count, custom slots, fixed measuring exclusion inversion

title: Pre-compute Voronoi diagrams at map ingestion for complex geometry features
description:
At map ingestion time, pre-compute high-granularity Voronoi partitions for non-Point features. This unblocks tentacles for LineString/Polygon categories (transit lines, coastlines, admin areas) and could improve matching/measuring performance.

Geometry handling:
- Points: no pre-computation needed (exact Voronoi at runtime)
- LineStrings: dense sampling along the line, Voronoi of samples, merge cells by parent feature
- Polygons: matching uses containment (ST_Contains) — no Voronoi needed. For measuring/tentacles, reduce to boundary (LineString) then sample.

Pre-computation avoids runtime approximation errors at Voronoi cell boundaries, which could produce incorrect game answers. Store pre-computed cells as Polygon geometries linked to each feature.

title: Randomize powerup: hider forces a random replacement question
description:
Hider plays a randomize powerup in response to any answerable question. Instead of answering, the server:
1. Notifies seekers that a randomize was played.
2. Seekers must choose (randomly — dice/RNG) a different unasked question from the same category. For slot-based questions (radar/thermometer), this means a different slot. For category-based (matching/measuring), this means a different category.
3. The randomly chosen replacement question is automatically asked, and the hider answers it normally.
4. The original question is NOT considered asked — it can be re-asked later at its original cost.

Key design points:
- Trust-based: no card/hand tracking. Hider assumed to have the powerup.
- The replacement must be from the same category but different parameters (e.g. 10mi radar → 50mi radar).
- If the replacement resolves to a null answer, that's valid (tough luck).
- The original slot/category is restored (not consumed).
- Auto-answer timer on the original question is revoked; a new timer starts on the replacement.
- Push flow: hider plays randomize → push to seekers → seekers pick random replacement → replacement is asked → hider answers.

Open questions:
- Should the server enforce randomness of the replacement, or trust the seekers to pick randomly?
- How to handle the intermediate state between randomize played and replacement selected?
- What if there are no other unasked questions in the same category?
close_reason: Server-side randomize powerup implemented and manually tested

title: Migrate mobile app from SwiftUI to React Native

title: Mobile: phase_changed SSE event not handled — UI stuck on hiding after timer expires
description: When the hiding timer expires and the server fires a phase_changed SSE event (hiding→seeking), the mobile client doesn't handle it. The GameplayStore has no handler for phase_changed — useGameplayEvents.ts only listens for game_state, player_location, and the question events. The UI stays on the hiding phase with 00:00:00 on the timer until the user force-closes and reopens (triggering a fresh SSE connection and full game_state hydrate). Fix: add a phase_changed listener that updates state.phase, seeking_started_at, station_election_status, and hider_station_id from the delta. Alternatively, the full game_state re-hydrate on reconnect already handles this — but the user shouldn't need to restart.
close_reason: Added phase_changed SSE handler in useGameplayEvents + applyPhaseChanged action in GameplayStore

title: Discipline test suite: mock DB in unit tests, reserve real DB for query/integration tests
description:
Unit tests currently import internal functions (e.g., `_buffer` from exclusion.py) and mix DB access into logic tests. This makes tests brittle and couples them to implementation details.

**Goals:**
- **Unit tests** (logic/, exclusion, conventions, geo): mock DB access (`get_session`, `register`, query functions). Test business logic in isolation with plain objects/fixtures.
- **Query tests**: use real DB (testcontainers PostGIS) to test query functions against actual SQL.
- **Integration tests** (via TestClient): use real DB, test full request→response flows through the router stack.
- Stop importing private/internal functions (e.g., `_buffer`) — test through public interfaces instead.
- Consider splitting test files to reflect the unit/query/integration boundary (e.g., `test_exclusion_unit.py` vs `test_exclusion_integration.py`, or subdirectories).

**Why:**
- Faster unit tests (no DB overhead for pure logic)
- Tests that break only when behavior changes, not when internals are refactored
- Clearer test boundaries matching the layered architecture (routers → logic → queries)
close_reason: Won't do

title: Replace timing JSON blob with real columns
description: Game.timing is an unstructured sa.JSON dict with string-key access and magic defaults (hiding_time_min=30, location_question_delay_min=5). Replace with proper typed columns on both Game and GameMap. Consumers should read real fields instead of .get() with fallback strings.

Two enhancements to the question selection UI (belt takeover):

1. **Browsing during active question**: When a question is active (waiting for answer), allow the seeker to open the question selection UI to browse types and parameters (preview boundaries eventually). Currently the 'Waiting' state disables the action button entirely. Should allow read-only browsing without the ability to submit.

2. **Back navigation in selection flow**: The Questions/action button should act as a contextual back button through the selection steps (custom → param → type → closed) rather than toggling straight to closed from any step. This gives the user a way to step back through the flow without losing their place.

title: Don't report seeker location updates until seeking has started
description: Seeker location updates are being reported/stored during the hiding phase before seeking begins. This leaks seeker position information to hiders prematurely and wastes resources tracking positions that aren't relevant to gameplay yet. Location updates for seekers should only be processed/broadcast once the seeking phase has actually started.

title: Veto powerup: hider refuses to answer a question
description:
Hider plays a veto powerup in response to any answerable question. The question goes unanswered — seekers are informed the hider used a veto but get no answer. The question is NOT considered consumed: seekers can re-ask the same question, but at multiplied cost (2x on second ask, 3x on third, etc.).

Key design points:
- Trust-based: no card/hand tracking on server. Hider is assumed to have the powerup.
- Veto replaces the answer action — hider hits a veto endpoint instead of the answer endpoint.
- Auto-answer timer must be revoked when veto is played (same as normal answer).
- Question status should reflect that it was vetoed (new status? or answered with a special answer value?).
- Push notification to seekers: "The hider used a veto! No answer this time."
- The re-ask cost multiplier mechanic (questions can be asked more than once, cost doubles each time) is a prerequisite — may need its own implementation work.

Open questions:
- Should vetoed questions have a distinct status (e.g. `vetoed`) or use `answered` with `answer=null`?
- How to track ask count per question identity for cost multiplier?
close_reason: Implemented veto endpoint, vetoed status, push event, tests, and docs

title: Support metric and imperial distance conventions
description: Games support both metric (meters/km) and imperial (miles) conventions. Radar/thermometer distance inventory differs between conventions (not a perfect conversion — e.g., 3km vs 2mi). The API surface must communicate distances in the selected convention so clients don't handle conversion/presentation.
close_reason: Implemented DistanceConvention enum, conventions.py module, field renames, conversion boundary in logic.py, code-level default inventory, imperial manual test script. All 143 tests pass.

title: Mobile: POP_TO_TOP toast on game end/dissolution navigation
description: When a game ends (dissolved or player leaves), useGameplayEvents calls router.dismissAll() then router.replace('/'). If the navigation stack is already flat (gameplay screen was reached via replace, not push), dismissAll triggers a POP_TO_TOP error toast. Fix: guard dismissAll with a navigation state check, or just use router.replace('/') without dismissAll since replace already handles the transition.
close_reason: Closed

title: Audit GET /games/{id} and GET /maps/{id} response sizes
description:
Both endpoints return everything in a single response and will grow with the data:

- GET /games/{id}: full inventory template (13 slots), all players, timing, timestamps. The inventory is static after game creation — no reason to re-send it every poll. Players rarely change after lobby.
- GET /maps/{id}: full boundary polygon (47+ pts), all district polygons (up to 144 pts each, 5 districts = ~450 pts), district_classes, full default_inventory. The boundary and districts are large geometry payloads that never change.

Consider:
1. Splitting static vs dynamic data (e.g., map geometry fetched once, game status polled frequently)
2. ETag/conditional GET for map data
3. Separate endpoints for heavy sub-resources (boundary, districts, inventory template)
4. Pagination or lazy loading for districts if maps grow to many districts

Not urgent for a single Seattle map and small games, but will matter if we add more maps or support larger player counts.
close_reason: Not a real concern — these endpoints are called infrequently

title: Mobile: Handle auto-assigned and ambiguous station election at phase transition
description: When the hiding phase ends and the station is auto_assigned or ambiguous, the mobile client needs to handle these transitions gracefully. Currently the stop selection UI (candidate stops, zone preview, Set Stop button) is tied to the hiding phase and clears on phase transition. For auto_assigned: the client should fetch and display the zone immediately (same as manual election). For ambiguous: the client should re-enter the stop selection flow during the seeking phase so hiders can resolve the ambiguity. Both cases need the phase_changed SSE delta (which carries station_election_status + hider_station_id) to drive the UI. See design/hider-station-election.md for spec.
close_reason: Implemented auto-assigned and ambiguous station handling at phase boundary (server + mobile)

title: Expand hiding zone powerup: increase hiding zone radius mid-game
description:
Hider plays a powerup to expand the hiding zone radius during the seeking phase. This makes it harder for seekers to narrow down the hider's location, since the candidate station pool grows and exclusion coverage becomes less effective relative to the larger zone.

Key design points:
- Trust-based: no card/hand tracking. Hider assumed to have the powerup.
- The hiding zone radius is currently implicit (derived from the hider's station and map geometry). This powerup would need an explicit radius override or multiplier on the game.
- Expansion should be a fixed increment or multiplier (e.g. +50%, or +X convention units). TBD what feels balanced.
- Can likely be played at any time during seeking, not just in response to a question.
- Affects candidate stations and endgame exclusion calculations — both use the hiding zone.
- Push notification to all players: "The hider has expanded the hiding zone!"
- Should there be a limit on how many times this can be played? (Probably trust-based — hider only has so many cards.)

Open questions:
- Fixed increment vs percentage multiplier for the expansion?
- Can it be stacked (played multiple times)?
- New endpoint: POST /games/{id}/expand-hiding-zone, or a generic powerup endpoint?
- How to store the override — new column on Game (e.g. hiding_zone_radius_multiplier)?
- Does the hider need to have reached seeking phase, or can they play it during hiding?
close_reason: Closed

title: Question history utility (hider + seeker)
description:
Add per-role question history UI accessible via utility belt.

Hider: read-only modal showing chronological list of questions (type, params, answer). Non-interactive.

Seeker: scrubber timeline with standalone map showing cumulative exclusion (red see-through) through scrub point + current question's delta exclusion (solid question-color, not rendered under already-excluded areas). Question card shows type/params/answer at current position.

## Design rationale

A general in-app notification/toast system (originally beads-466) was explored and ruled out because existing visual affordances already command attention for question lifecycle events:
- Hiders see a colored bar during active questions (type, timer, answer buttons).
- Seekers see a banner for each active question with timer.
- On answer, the map updates.

So the user attention problem is already solved for question events. What's actually missing is a way to *review* past questions — hence this history utility. A narrow toast feature (beads-035) still covers non-obvious non-question events (player-left, host-change, zone-expanded).

## Key files

- mobile/src/components/QuestionCutoffModal.tsx — existing seeker endgame cutoff modal; reference for row rendering and map-with-exclusions pattern.
- mobile/src/components/utility-belt/UtilityBelt.tsx — utility belt container. Currently holds 'Powers' (hider) and 'Endgame' (seeker). New history entry slots in alongside.
- mobile/src/stores/GameplayStore — holds question_history array, already populated from SSE stream.
- core/src/hideandseek_core/broadcast/events.py — HiderQuestionAnsweredEvent / SeekerQuestionAnsweredEvent carry all needed data.

## Shared refactor

Extract a QuestionHistoryRow component from QuestionCutoffModal so all three surfaces render identically: seeker endgame cutoff, hider history modal, seeker scrubber question card.

## Data

title: Clean up response schemas: eliminate noise nulls and tighten write responses
description:
Several API responses return fields that are always null/meaningless in context:

1. **QuestionDetailResponse (write endpoints)**: When returned from ask/answer POSTs, fields like seeker_location_end, hider_location, answered_at, answer are all null on ask, and seeker_location_end is null for non-thermometer types always. 2. **answerable_at on radar questions**: Always ~0.1ms after asked_at (meaningless). This field only matters for thermometers. Could omit for non-thermometer types.

3. **GameResponse nulls in early states**: hiding_started_at and seeking_started_at are null in lobby/hiding. join_code persists into seeking (should be nulled at transition — it already is in the DB but only when the game ends, not at seeking start).

These are cosmetic but they make the API feel unpolished and force the client to handle many null cases that conceptually can't happen.

title: Migrate marchese.dev nameservers from Squarespace to Route 53
description:

title: Deploy HideAndSeek to production
description:
Get the HideAndSeek stack deployed to a real hosted environment so external users can play.

## Scope
The monorepo currently runs locally via docker compose (PostGIS + Redis + FastAPI + Celery worker + reconciler) and mobile via Expo dev builds. This epic covers everything needed to move that to a hosted deployment:

- **Backend hosting**: pick a platform (Fly.io, Railway, Render, AWS ECS, GKE, etc.) and deploy the FastAPI server, Celery worker, and reconciler services.
- **Database**: managed PostGIS (RDS, Supabase, Neon-with-postgis, Crunchy Bridge, etc.) with backups and migrations strategy.
- **Redis**: managed Redis (Upstash, ElastiCache, etc.) for Celery broker + SSE pub/sub.
- **Secrets/config**: DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, APNs key, FCM service account, etc. — pick a secret store.
- **CI/CD**: build + deploy pipeline (GitHub Actions → registry → platform).
- **Domain + TLS**: register domain, wire DNS, terminate TLS.
- **Observability**: logs, metrics, error tracking (Sentry?), uptime checks.
- **Mobile distribution**: EAS build + submit for TestFlight / Play internal testing; point app at hosted API URL via env config.
- **Push credentials in prod**: production APNs key + FCM service account wired into hosted env.
- **GTFS data pipeline**: how/when the Seattle GTFS import runs against the prod DB.
- **Smoke/manual tests against hosted env**: adapt `scripts/manual-test.sh` to run against a staging URL.

## Out of scope (for now)
- Multi-region / HA beyond what the chosen platform gives by default
- Autoscaling tuning (basic fixed sizing is fine for first deploy)
- Public launch / marketing

## Deliverable
A documented, reproducible deployment where a fresh clone + a few commands (or a merged PR) results in a running staging environment reachable by a TestFlight/internal-track build of the mobile app.
design:
See [design/2026-04-19-aws-deployment.md](../design/2026-04-19-aws-deployment.md) for the full deployment architecture.

**Summary of decisions** (open questions in the epic description are now answered there):

- Platform: **AWS** with **CDK (TypeScript)** for IaC
- Compute: **ECS Fargate** for server, worker, and reconciler
- Database: **Aurora Serverless v2 Postgres** (min 0 ACU), PostGIS enabled
- Cache/broker: **ElastiCache Redis** (`cache.t4g.micro`)
- Push: **SNS Mobile Push** replaces direct APNs + FCM (removes `aioapns` and `firebase-admin`)
- Ingress: **CloudFront → ALB (IPv6-only) → Fargate**
- Egress: **IPv6-only** via Egress-Only IGW (no NAT gateway, no interface endpoints)
- Domain: **hideandseek.marchese.dev** (Route 53 hosted zone created by CDK; manual nameserver update at Squarespace)
- Region: us-west-2
- Estimated cost: ~$59/mo always-on idle, ~$34/mo with Fargate scaled to 0

See the design doc's 'Implementation Phases' section for the sequence; child issues should be filed per-phase.

title: CloudFront + hideandseek.marchese.dev alias

title: Mobile: Question history interactions
description:
Design + build interactions for browsing and scrubbing the seeker's question history on mobile.

## Context
The "context strip" concept from design/utility-belt.md §2 was abandoned. What remains worth building is the **question history timeline** — the ability for seekers (and possibly hiders, TBD) to review past questions/answers and see how the map's exclusion state evolved.

Static hider station name display (also originally in the context strip) is either dropped or lives somewhere else in the UI — decide during design.

## Needs design
This epic needs a design doc before implementation. Open questions:
- Where does history live in the UI? (Dedicated screen, sheet, overlay, inline with map?)
- What interactions does scrubbing support? Tap-to-jump, scrub, play-through animation?
- What does scrubbing show on the map? Snapshot of total_exclusion at that point, or just the question's own delta?
- Does the hider see any version of this, or seeker-only?
- How does "current" vs "historical" state read visually — color, overlay, banner?
- Does endgame action still live at the end of the timeline, or move elsewhere?

## Out of scope
- Context strip component itself (abandoned)
- Hider station name display (handle separately)

## Deliverable
Design doc → implementation tasks filed as children of this epic.
close_reason: Superseded by HideAndSeek-qpr, which resolves the open design questions (hider modal + seeker scrubber) and has implementation children filed (0r6, urs).

title: Support MultiPolygon boundaries on GameMap
description:
Change GameMap.boundary column from POLYGON to GEOMETRY to support both Polygon and MultiPolygon boundaries.

Scope:
- models/game_map.py: change column type from ShapelyGeometry('POLYGON') to ShapelyGeometry('GEOMETRY')
- schemas/response.py: change GeoJSONPolygon to GeoJSONGeometry for boundary fields (MapDetail, EffectiveMapResponse, HiderGameStateResponse, SeekerGameStateResponse)
- queries/game_state.py: update boundary serialization to use geom_or_none or _geojson_adapter
- queries/stops.py: verify ST_Contains works with MultiPolygon (it does)
- exclusion.py: verify hiding zone computation handles MultiPolygon boundary
- Tests: verify both Polygon and MultiPolygon boundaries work
- seed_seattle_map.py: may need MultiPolygon for island/water-body maps
close_reason: Closed

title: Mobile: Hider randomize power UI on active question
description: Add a 'Randomize' action to the hider's active question UI during seeking phase. When a question is answerable, the hider should see a randomize option alongside answer/veto. Calls POST /questions/{id}/randomize. On success, the client receives a QuestionAskedEvent while an active question exists — infer this as a randomize (the old question transitions to 'randomized' status). No special animation needed initially — just show the new question. Should disable the button if no eligible replacement slots exist (requires checking inventory for same-type slots with ask_count == 0).
